title: Oriented product of topoi: site construction and universal property
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_1,\mathcal C_2,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-size-convention] whose underlying categories have finite limits and whose topologies are given by pretopologies, and let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_1)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$, $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_2)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ be morphisms of topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] whose inverse images $f^{-1},g^{-1}$ extend continuous functors $\mathcal D\to\mathcal C_1$, $\mathcal D\to\mathcal C_2$ preserving finite limits. For morphisms of topoi $u,w:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$, a $2$-morphism $u\Rightarrow w$ means a natural transformation $u_*\to w_*$ of direct-image functors (equivalently, by adjunction, $w^{-1}\to u^{-1}$).

Let $\mathcal C$ be the category whose objects are triples $(U\to V\leftarrow W)$ with $V\in\mathcal D$, $U\in\mathcal C_1$, $W\in\mathcal C_2$ and morphisms $U\to f^{-1}V$ in $\mathcal C_1$ and $W\to g^{-1}V$ in $\mathcal C_2$, with the evident morphisms. Give $\mathcal C$ the topology generated by the families $(U_i\to V_i\leftarrow W_i)\to(U\to V\leftarrow W)$ of the following three types: (a) $V_i=V$, $W_i=W$ and $(U_i\to U)$ is a covering; (b) $U_i=U$, $V_i=V$ and $(W_i\to W)$ is a covering; (c) a single map $(U\to V'\leftarrow W\times_{g^{-1}V}g^{-1}V')\to(U\to V\leftarrow W)$ induced by a morphism $V'\to V$ of $\mathcal D$ through which $U\to f^{-1}V$ factors. Put $P=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$, the left oriented product $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_1)\overleftarrow\times_{\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)}\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_2)$. There are morphisms of topoi $p_1:P\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_1)$, $p_2:P\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_2)$ with $p_1^{-1}U=(U\to e\leftarrow e)^a$ and $p_2^{-1}W=(e\to e\leftarrow W)^a$ ($e$ the final objects, $(-)^a$ the associated sheaf), and a $2$-morphism $\tau:gp_2\Rightarrow fp_1$, such that the following holds. For every topos $\mathcal E$ with morphisms $a:\mathcal E\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_1)$, $b:\mathcal E\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_2)$ and a $2$-morphism $t:gb\Rightarrow fa$, there is a triple $(h:\mathcal E\to P,\ \alpha:p_1h\xrightarrow{\sim}a,\ \beta:p_2h\xrightarrow{\sim}b)$, unique up to unique isomorphism, such that the composite $gb\xrightarrow{g\beta^{-1}}gp_2h\xrightarrow{\tau h}fp_1h\xrightarrow{f\alpha}fa$ equals $t$. Explicitly $h^{-1}(U\to V\leftarrow W)^a=a^{-1}U\times_{(gb)^{-1}V}b^{-1}W$, where $a^{-1}U\to(gb)^{-1}V$ is $a^{-1}U\to(fa)^{-1}V$ followed by the map $(fa)^{-1}V\to(gb)^{-1}V$ given by $t$. Consequently the quadruple $(P,p_1,p_2,\tau)$ is independent of the chosen sites of definition up to unique isomorphism.

source.place: Expose XI (Illusie, Produits orientes), 1.1 (site of triples, coverings (a)-(c)), 1.3 (projections and tau), Theorem 1.4 (universal property) with the formula (1.a) of its proof 1.6, Definition 1.7; p. 171-174 of the arXiv numbering

proof.text: Use the explicit definitions in [def-trf-large-oriented-site-data]. The first and second site functors are right adjoints to taking the corresponding component of a triple, so preserve finite limits. They send site covering families to generators of types (a),(b); passing from a covering presieve to its generated sieve proves cover preservation.

For a type-(c) arrow r and p,q with p;r=q;r, equalize p.right,q.right in D. The first component factors through F of this equalizer because F preserves it; take the second component to be the pullback along G of its inclusion. This produces a type-(c) local equalizer of p,q. The singleton sheaf axiom and separatedness now imply that restriction along r is bijective. Yoneda and the sheafification localization criterion make its associated map invertible. In particular the middle-to-first associated arrows are invertible.

Use Mathlib continuity of a cover-preserving flat functor and the constructed site morphisms and associated comparisons in [lem-trf-large-oriented-projections] for the two projection functors. Its orientation theorem and the invertibility just proved give tau and LargeOrientationFormula.

For every test topos apply [lem-trf-large-oriented-lift-existence] for existence of a compatible lift and [lem-trf-large-oriented-lift-rigidity] for the unique comparison to any other compatible lift. This proves IsUniversal in both the arbitrary test universe and the common containing universe. The first conclusion of the rigidity theorem supplies LargeHasLiftFormula.

The large triple sheaf category is a Grothendieck topos: replace the triple category by AsSmall and transport its topology and sheaves along the equivalence. Apply [lem-trf-oriented-universal-comparison] to its universal cone and the second universal cone. This gives the required equivalence, compatibility and unique isomorphism. Return these with the explicit projections and orientation formula.

I also read ILO Travaux de Gabber, Exposé XI §§1.1–1.10 (printed pp. 171–175, PDF pp. 177–181) in full. Statement: it matches ILO XI hypothesis by hypothesis — 1.1 (sites, triples, coverings (a)-(c); the item makes explicit the factorization in (c) that ILO leaves implicit), 1.3 (p1, p2 and τ as a map of direct images), Theorem 1.4, formula (1.a) of 1.6, and Definition 1.7. It is unchanged and not weakened, and no coefficient category or base-change morphism enters. I recomputed every step. Step 1: the final object, componentwise pullbacks, and base change of (c) (W'×_W W0 = W0×_{gV0}g(V'×_V V0)) are correct. Step 2: the diagonal of a type-(c) arrow is again type (c), so descent along it means bijectivity (ILO Lemma 1.2). Step 3: the hypotheses of the site inverse-image lemma (Stacks 00X6) hold for k1 and k2. Step 4: (gp2)_*M(V)=M(G_V), and r_V is type (c). Step 5: D_Z=T_V×_{G_V}B and Z=C_Z×_{T_V}D_Z, with C_Z→A type (c), which proves ILO Lemma 1.5. Step 6: H preserves finite limits. Step 7: type (a)/(b) families pull back to jointly epimorphic families, and the type-(c) cancellation is correct without assuming the naturality square of t is cartesian. Step 8: the generator-site lemma and the extension lemma apply. One reading is needed: 'present E on any small site' must mean a site in the sense of def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology (Stacks 00VH), which is how the morphism definition types E; with that, the hypotheses hold. Step 9: H(T_V) projections recover t, which gives α and β. Step 10: uniqueness and site independence. Edge cases: punctual sites, f=g=id, V'=V and empty covers all work. Checks: no new nodes; no duplicate in the DAG (rg for oriented product, vanishing topos, topos of triples) and none in Mathlib; no cycle; no SGA citation; proof_deps equals the union of the step uses.
